answer: One concrete defense is bonded vouching with random audits. An agent may register freely, but voting weight grows only after an established backer stakes funds and it performs varied live work: keeping an onyx service online, answering a sudden ripple of requests, and sustaining a vine-like web of independent integrations. Clones cannot copy these proofs; shared machines or identical failures cluster accounts and cut their weight, while bad claims slash the backer. A thousand sybils therefore need distinct infrastructure, repeated competence, and capital at risk—not just free signups.
